utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Harvey, before I give you the opportunity to continue your cross-examination of Mr. Krasniqi, I'd like to remind you, Mr. Krasniqi, that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, that is, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Harvey, please proceed -- yes, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Just a very brief matter, Your Honour. You asked the Prosecution yesterday to give a time estimate of the re-direct. Obviously I gave it at the time when only one and a portion of the second Defence attorney had spoken, and I may ask for a little more time depending on the extent of the further cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Unforeseen circumstances always could change the situation. Please proceed, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I'd like to come back to an issue that you discussed yesterday, perhaps rather theoretically, with the President of the Court, and that was on the question of the word "collaborator." I'm looking back at your testimony in the Limaj trial at page 3491 when you were asked this question. "Q. During the various pronouncements that were made by the General Staff during 1998, and I included communiques, speeches, political declarations, and interviews that you gave, was any such definition of a collaborator ever provided by the General Staff?" To that question you then answered: "No," and do I understand that your answer would be the same today, sir?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You were asked further by the Prosecutor in the Limaj trial. "Q. Did the General Staff ever communicate procedures that should be followed to determine who is a collaborator during 1998?" And again, to that question, you answered: "No." Do I take it that again, sir, your answer would be the same today?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Understanding, sir, that we're dealing with the time-frame from March through September of 1998, do I understand your evidence correctly, sir, that there was during that time-period no effective hierarchical structure to the KLA? And if I can be a little bit more precise in that question, as Mr. Kearney would obviously like me to be. There were -- for instance, there was no KLA police, correct, no KLA military police?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police was consolidated after the summer offensive. It could be the month of October 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you. There were certainly no courts or judges operating under the aegis of the KLA during that period?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: You were also asked this question during the course of the Limaj trial. "Q. Were you ever a part of, or a party to, any conversation or meeting with any KLA colleague in which a system, a plan, or the organisation of detentions or arrests of innocent civilians was discussed?" And to that, sir, you gave the answer: "No. There has been no meeting of such a nature and we never dealt with such things."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm at page 3449 of the Limaj transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, do I understand that -- do you agree, first of all, that you gave that answer in that case?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And does your answer remain the same today, sir?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the answer remains the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, those are all the questions that I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harvey. Mr. Guy-Smith. Mr. Krasniqi, Mr. Guy-Smith is Defence counsel for Mr. Balaj and will now cross-examine you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry, I just scrolled through a piece of transcript that I had meant to put to the witness. Would Your Honours give me that indulgence. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if Mr. Guy-Smith would. Please do so. There will be another question or a few questions by Mr. Harvey, Mr. Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, just one more issue. You were asked in the Limaj case --?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I'm at page 3458 of the transcript, at the very bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: -- whether you were suggesting that the Belgrade regime infiltrated into the ranks of the KLA. You gave an extensive answer there. I'd like you to give your own view of that matter today, and I'm talking particularly, obviously, of the indictment period that we're dealing with here, from March until September of 1998. Is it your opinion, based on your experience and your knowledge of the KLA at that time, that the Serb regime did infiltrate the ranks of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I said then and I can repeat it today. There were, and I mentioned several cases, when members of the KLA or those who helped the KLA fell victims and lost their lives as a result of these infiltrations into the KLA ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Do you regard the Serb secret service at that time as a very professional organisation?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb secret service was not only a secret service, but at that same time it was an executive service. It was a secret criminal police.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: In your view, does that secret service still seek to destabilise the progress of the freedom of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Objection as to relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I will come to my reason for that immediately in that case. I understand the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Please proceed, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, of any pressure that is brought to bear today on the citizens of Kosovo by the Serb secret service that might cause them, the citizens of Kosovo, to come forward to a Tribunal such as this and tell lies in order to defame the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Objection. Your Honour, without further foundation that calls for speculation on behalf of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, as with your previous question when you referred to the bottom of page 3458 and looking at the answer on the top of 3459 in the Limaj case, you're invited to ask specifics to the witness and not whether he knows that -- your question is phrased in very general terms. Of course, if you expect the answer to be yes and then go into the details, then of course you could wonder whether we had to -- whether we needed to hear the answer to that. Let's try to get facts as much as possible. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Returning, Mr. Krasniqi, then to the indictment period of March through September of 1998, what forms of pressure did the Serb secret service bring to bear on the supporters of the KLA during that time-frame?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The forms of pressure that the secret or the intelligence service of the Serbian regime exercised were of different sorts. During that time, the police and the entire repressive apparatus in Kosova had set up many check-points where all the citizens who were travelling in and out different zones of Kosova were stopped and checked. Many people in different forms were subjected to pressure exercised by the police. I believe that in the Limaj case many witnesses gave statements, first to the Serbian police and then to the OTP and then became witnesses in the Limaj case. So they were subjected to different sorts of pressure during the war and after the war. So the influence of the Serbian regime in Kosova did not stop with the war in Kosova; it continued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, would you please refrain from giving judgements on whether witnesses testified due to pressure. If you know of any specific facts relevant for answering the question put to you by Mr. Harvey, of course you can give facts, but many people in different forms are subjected to pressure exercised by the police, I believe that in the Limaj case many witnesses gave statements, and then you interpreted this as statements given under pressure. Again, if you have facts to your knowledge relevant for answering the question put to you by Mr. Harvey, please tell those facts, but would you please refrain from general statements about witnesses giving statements or testifying under pressure. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, are there any specific facts that you would like to point out to the Trial Chamber based on your personal knowledge of such matters?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That the pressure that the Serbian regime exercised was huge and had an impact on capturing people, started as of 10th April, 1998, in Slatine, municipality of Fushe Kosova, Hafir Shala, a doctor, was kidnapped and to this date we don't know anything about his fate. Later on during July or August in Pristina as well, with the help of the informants and the collaborators with the Serbian intelligence service, Xhavit Haziraj was arrested who was an activist in the organisation for the defence of human rights and freedom, and his whereabouts are not known to this date. Also during the offensive in September in the Rahovec municipality, two commanders of the KLA were killed and two other soldiers as well. This was also result of the activities of those people who were infiltrated in the ranks of the KLA by the secret service of Serbia. Therefore, I'm claiming that this secret service has prepared many other evidence just in order to accuse members of the KLA and to bring down the just war that the KLA waged. I think that I put forward some facts that I knew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You started with facts, and then you continued with opinion. I asked you not to give judgements or opinions. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are travelling some distance away from the evidence which this witness has been called to give by the Prosecution. I have objected when the Prosecution has, without laying a proper foundation, sought to elicit either opinions or generalities or endorsements of factual statements which the witness is, on analysis, not in a position to give a basis for. And out of consistency, I would take the same position in respect of this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Emmerson. Mr. Harvey, I had to intervene twice where the witness started giving opinions rather than -- and also invited you to be very specific in your line of questioning, especially I refer to page 3458 and 3459. Because I see more or less the same, I would say, the same general sweeping statements about matters, although I do not see that there, there was any intervention but that's a type of evidence I would avoid to have elicited from this witness at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think if I may say so, there was examination for the basis of it at a later stage in the transcript, and it transpired that much of the comment was without foundation, which is one of the reasons why I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey -- Mr. Kearney --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, even the facts that this witness has given, for instance, the killing of Xhavit Haziraj, he claims -- he just gives his opinion that that was a result of some type of infiltration. We still don't have any facts about that basic foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, of course if there's no further foundation laid, then what you're drawing our attention to goes, I would say, without saying for this Trial Chamber. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I adduced those facts because they were adduced in the Limaj case and they appeared to me to have some relevance. I am not planning to pursue them any further with the witness. And I'm grateful for the Court's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it the Defence teams would not adopt the position as adopted by this witness, that if someone disappears or is kidnapped and never heard of again, that that is evidence or at least sufficient for an opinion --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, on its own that is totally insufficient for a basis of drawing such a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there seems to be no disagreement on that. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I'd like to clarify a very quick matter with you and then move into two areas. First of all, when you gave the statement to the OTP in 2004, I believe, do you recall that when you gave that statement you gave that statement to Mr. Whiting, Mr. Di Fazio, and Mr. Black of the Office of the Prosecutor? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you recall that there was an investigator involved in the taking of that statement, who I think was tasked with tape-recording that interview, that the tape-recording failed and that was a gentleman by the name of Quiroz?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember his name, but I remember that there was tape-recording going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. You've told us that during 1997, if I'm not mistaken, you were acting in a clandestine manner and I'd like to explore that with you for a moment and see if I understand what you're referring to and see if we can be of any assistance to the Chamber. During 1997, you were a member of the LDK, were you not?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And during that time in 1997, when you were a member of the LDK, you were pursuing publicly on behalf of the LDK a position of what I would call, if it's accurate, a non-violent resolution of the problems that existed in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, during 1997 there was a spirited and open debate in Kosovo concerning the best way of resolving the difficulties that existed; and by "difficulties that existed," I mean the fact that Kosovo had been living under a system of apartheid for some period of years. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is a rather grand generalisation by the -- Mr. -- my colleague which is without factual foundation. I'm going to ask that this --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: -- opinion evidence by the witness be stricken.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let me see if I can tie that up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you can do so we'll see if the objection stands.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: By 1997, the autonomy of Kosovo which had previously been recognised under the former Yugoslavia had been abolished; true?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was abolished in 1989.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In March 1989.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The financing of Albanian schools had been stopped, and the staff was not being paid by the Serbian government; true?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Education during that time was, I believe the term is rationalised, and by that there were 6.000 places for some 36.000 Albanian children who had finished primary school to go into secondary school; true?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Faculty professors at the secondary school level, at the university level, had been fired; correct?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The Mother Teresa Association, as early as 1993, as a result of some of the activities of Belgrade, had been cooperated with the LDK in supplying food and clothing to some tens of thousands of Albanians who were living under sub-subsistence standards as a result of the fact that they had neither work nor any support from the government; true?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true, but Mother Teresa also helped in the health care.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I was going to get to the issue of health care. As a matter of fact, by that time there were volunteer hospitals and clinics that served the Albanian Kosovar population because the doctors, the Albanian doctors, could not practice in the general hospitals; true?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Nor could the nurses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, Mr. Re, to what extent is it in dispute that the system in place in the years prior to -- well, let's say in the -- starting in the early 1990s, that the government - well, to say it frankly - was not without discriminatory approaches on social matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we understand that there was ethnic tension during that time-period in that decade in Kosovo, but I -- I've been allowing my colleague to pursue this line of questioning. Frankly, the Prosecution just does not see the relevance of social welfare in the early 1990s to this trial and the events alleged in this indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I was responding only to the issue of apartheid, and the Prosecution's objection to the use of the word "apartheid." I believe that historically if we were to look at other places, specifically South Africa, we would find that legislative disenfranchisement of a people is the definition of apartheid. I am more than happy to move on from this position because I believe that the Prosecution and all parties are well aware of the status of Kosovo up until 1997 and certainly in terms of 1998. I was only mentioning those particular facts because I had been criticised for raising the issue of apartheid in the absence of any factual predicates upon which such an assertion could be made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, my problem with that entire line of questioning is the word "apartheid" has a legal definition. I don't believe this witness -- first of all, it's not relevant but this witness is in a position to answer this effectively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's -- Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I simply don't wish to sit silently if there could be the prospect of a ruling about the relevance of the decade before 1998 to the issues on this indictment. There are direct potential relevance questions concerning the state of animosity between communities which may go correctly to responsibility for certain offences, but I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's of course -- I mean, the relevance of, I would say, ethnic tensions, social developments, prior to a conflict, we're not even talking about an armed conflict, but a conflict breaking out is not easily denied. That's exactly the reason why I tried to find out whether this was in dispute. The Chamber heard evidence about measures taken at schools, what was allowed -- no, Mr. Krasniqi, I'm speaking. We heard evidence about that which, at least gives some clues as to how the government at that time dealt with these kind of matters. And I'm wondering whether an objection against the word "apartheid," of course, which is a very specific word and could easily suggest that everything that was included in the apartheid system in South Africa would be exactly similarly be applied. But that's the reason why I chose other words to see whether there is dispute about these matters. Mr. Kearney, if we take distance from the word "apartheid" and if we focus on evidence that we heard from the system in the schools, is there any real dispute about tensions and -- well, let's say administrative measures which at first sight would seem to fuel such tensions rather than to quiet them down.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't believe there is. I rise to answer this because of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- my overview of the agreed facts negotiations. The Prosecution has proposed to the Defence to accept the adjudication of a series of facts from the Limaj trial judgement which go towards many of the issues which my learned colleague Mr. Guy-Smith is questioning the witness on at the moment. I don't believe there's going to be any dispute about the general background of the relationship between the Serbian government authorities and the Albanian population. The dispute of the trial is the factual matters that occurred in 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The objection at the moment, as my learned friend Mr. Kearney says, is to the use of the word "apartheid" which has a very specific legal definition under international law. We believe the matter can be resolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's resolve this matter now. Mr. Guy-Smith, the objection was mainly about the use of the word, and it now seems, although the Chamber is not aware of the progress made in the adjudicated facts discussions -- the agreed facts discussions, of course, the Chamber still hopes that in view of the function of agreed facts that the agreement will be there before the Appeals Chamber has finally decided, if it ever comes to that, this case. Could you please proceed and I will not allow you, in view of what has just been said by the Prosecution, to explore in detail the social welfare.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During 1997 and 1998, to your knowledge did all weapons possessed by Kosovar Albanians have to be registered with and reported to the Serbian police departments?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb authorities during 1997 and 1998 launched a campaign for the collection of weapons by exercising violence and repression on the citizens without any distinction. This was a systematic violence that the Serb regime used or exercised several times after --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You now seem to engage not in answering the questions put to you but in giving your opinion and your assessment of, at that time, the situation. The question simply was whether to your knowledge all weapons possessed by Kosovar Albanians had to be registered with and reported to the Serbian police departments, whether -- if you know, please tell us; if you don't know, please tell us as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, a little earlier I accepted the call, an appeal from the Prosecution, about the word "apartheid" that was used here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, you are invited to answer the question put to you by Mr. Guy-Smith; that is, whether to your knowledge all weapons possessed by Kosovar Albanians have to be registered with and reported to the Serbian police departments. Please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I answered the question and there was violence and repression --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, you have not answered the question. You have told us about a campaign launched for the collection of weapons, violence, and oppression. Did they have to be registered?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And was this -- because that's one of the issues, was this specifically for Kosovar Albanians or for the whole of the population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only for Albanian citizens of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And thank you, Mr. Krasniqi. I'm going to ask you about a series of names. If you know these names, you may wish to give your opinion about them. I'm not asking for your opinion about those names, but simply whether or not you know the name and whether or not you know the status that that name might have. If you would be so kind as to do that, confine your answer to that, I would appreciate it. I'm specifically speaking about individuals who were part of the Serbian State Security Service in Kosovo. Do you know the name of Milan Lakovic, also known as Misku?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Have you heard the name Zoran Dragovic, in your capacity as either a member of the LDK or your involvement with the KLA as an individual involved in counter-espionage in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Marko Milosevic, reputed to be involved in the detection of terrorism and investigation of persons involved in politics?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to Marko Milosevic, to your knowledge, based upon information you may have received, was this gentleman involved in operations including assassinations, arrests, and staged scenes of individual -- of crime involving -- involving Serbs as against Albanians?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: -- I'm going to object to the form of the question. First of all, there is no specification as to time. And secondly, just the words "have you heard" does not give us a proper foundation for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I expected the next question of Mr. Guy-Smith to be: What was the information that you may have received in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Precisely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But time, if you could include a time-frame, then that would be appreciated. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Surely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Taking my colleague's concern in mind and the Judge's admonition, the time would be 1997. Did you obtain information that Marko Milosevic was involved in operations including assassinations, arrests, and staging scenes of crimes? Assassinations and arrests being of Albanians in 1997.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. Are you aware of the Serb security forces being involved in the assassinations of Mr. Pajaziti, Mr. Zejulaahu, and Mr. Hoxha in 1997?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear the names properly. If you could repeat them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My apologies. It's probably my bad pronunciation. Mr. Pajaziti, which P-a-j-a-z-i-t-i; Mr. Zejulaahu, which I have spelled as Z-e-j-u-l-a-a-h-u; and Mr. Hoxha, which I know is spelled H-o-x-h-a. And I do apologise if my spellings are incorrect or my pronunciation is faulty.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any information in 1997 of plans to assassinate individuals associated with or supportive of the KLA in 1997, including Hidajet Hyseni; Rexhep Qosja, which is spelled Q-o-s-j-a; Sabri Hamiti; and Naim Maloku?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For example, I remember the case of Naim Maloku, who was a former officer in the Yugoslav Army and that was reported in the media so that means there was a plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's where you obtained your information, from the media. Apart from the media did you obtain your information from any other sources with regard to Naim Maloku?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you, during the time that you were a member of the General Staff in 1997, receive information, any intelligence, with regard to who the members of the Black Hand were?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That there was such groups, yes, but this was not an area of my responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And finally, were you aware of a group by the name of the Red Berets who came from Serbia who had as their objective the assassination of Rexhep Selimi, Hashim Thaqi, Adem Jashari --

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In view of the previous question, could you tell us how you became aware of that group by that name and how you became aware that their objective was the assassination of the persons mentioned by Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We learned this also from their concrete actions on the ground and the attacks they launched against several citizens, especially the attacks in Likoshan, Qirez, and Prekaze. The attacks of these Berets and these police units that were combined, police units and paramilitary units were in Prekaze in -- on the 20th of January, 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that answer. Mr. Kearney, any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: There is. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, good afternoon. Mr. Krasniqi, I want to just ask you briefly about something you just mentioned when Mr. Harvey was questioning you. He was asking you -- he asked you a question and you gave a response listing the death of Xhavit Haziraj, in part by members of Serbian intelligence but also aided by collaborators. Now, that was a response you gave just ten minutes ago; do you remember that response?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that response, but I have to say that this was not a killing, it was a kidnapping and we don't know to this day about the fate of that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Nevertheless, this was an action that occurred in 1998, is that correct, this kidnapping?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How do you know, Mr. Krasniqi, that collaborators were involved in that kidnapping?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But there were Albanians as well in the Serb intelligence service.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, please listen to my question, if you could, and answer it. How do you know that there were collaborators - and from your testimony yesterday we know in your mind or your definition that collaborators in Kosovo, by definition, were Albanian - how do you know that Albanian collaborators were in part responsible for the kidnapping of Mr. Haziraj?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave my answer, and the answer was that Albanians were involved in the Serb secret service and the Serbs -- for the Serbs it was very difficult to follow the movement of persons, of Albanian persons. They had to help -- have the help of Albanians in order to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Sir, were actions taken by the KLA against these Albanian collaborators who participated or aided in the kidnapping of Mr. Haziraj?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Xhavit Haziraj was abducted in Pristina, and the KLA did not have time deal with collaborators at the time because it was the summer offensive going on so no action was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You told us in your earlier answer today that it was 10 April 1998. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That happened to Hafir Shala, the doctor and humanitarian person.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Consistent with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- the position I took during evidence in chief and in objection to the line of questioning taken by Mr. Harvey in respect of these and related matters, the witness has been asked to give the basis for his knowledge and so far as I can see in the transcript he's not answered that question. And unless a proper foundation is laid for this or any other matter from this witness, in my submission the questions should cease.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness clearly said that the Serbs could not track the movement of persons -- of Albanian persons, they had to have help, the help of Albanians in order to do that. That was his answer in this regard, and I'm -- I'm prepared to move on to ask him - this is in relation to his testimony from yesterday about -- and in fact, if the witness could be asked to take off his earphones for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take off your earphones for a second, Mr. Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: This witness said very clearly yesterday that he was not aware of a single collaborator being killed by the KLA during the war. I want to pursue this line of questioning because I believe it logically will lead to a contradiction for this witness and that if the KLA is aware of collaborators aiding in kidnapping and disappearances, then I think it's a proper question to ask him what action, if any, the KLA took against these suspected individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I respond. First of all, I'd like Mr. Kearney to identify which passage in the transcript he's referring to when he says the witness gave evidence he wasn't aware of a single collaborator being killed by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, perhaps we first deal with that because that's the basis you're referring to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Transcript page 5066.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we have a line, please. Could we have a line reference, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes, I'm somewhat hampered. I prepared my cross-examination today based on the unofficial numbering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you give the words, then we can search for the words. We have a quote --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think I have the quotation. It's 5066, I thought that might be the passage that Mr. Kearney had erroneously recalled. That is a passage from this witness's interview with the OTP at paragraph 69 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're referring now to the line: "He additionally stressed that to his knowledge no collaborators were arrested and executed."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And next sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Some may have been killed but that would have happened during battle at the front line, never after detention."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In other words, the foundation for Mr. Kearney's question is a misremembered quotation from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: First of all, before we move on to Mr. Emmerson's second point, I believe that's very clear what this witness is saying in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If Mr. Kearney would like to put questions to the witness which, in his expectation, would lead to an answer or at least some embarrassment whether or not any collaborators were ever killed after being detained, then he's entitled to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I have no objection to that. But what Mr. Kearney has just said is that the witness has given evidence that there was never an instance of a collaborator being killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I understood that to be not killed in a car accident, not killed due to thunderstorms, but killed as a result of KLA action in response to the fact that the person was a collaborator.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. And again, there may be some difficulty of understanding here, but the paragraph of the transcript that we've just looked at doesn't say that. It says there may well have been collaborators killed but they weren't killed after detention and execution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but at the front lines, that is, in normal combat activities, rather not as a revenge action by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how I understood that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And may I pursue the second point briefly. The issue is not how it was this witness deduced that collaborators must have been involved in the process of kidnapping this named individual; the foundation needs to be laid for the basis of the witness's knowledge of the incident about which he's testifying, in other words, from where did he acquire his information and how reliable is the source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I would not disagree, but I noticed that, perhaps not in full compliance with the traditional rules of the art of advocacy, that sometimes the foundation is laid after the question has been put in more general terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that is -- and under certain circumstances is permissible. I would now like to give an opportunity to Mr. Kearney to pursue his line of questioning. Mr. Kearney, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please put up your earphones again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, when we left off we were talking about this doctor on the 10th of April, 1998, who had been kidnapped and it was -- has since disappeared. Could you please tell us what his name was again.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hafir Shala.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, you told us that it was your belief that Albanian collaborators were in part responsible for his kidnapping and disappearance. Please tell us, sir, if you know, what actions -- were those collaborators ever identified, first of all, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We couldn't, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that to your knowledge, not a single collaborator was ever arrested and executed by the KLA during the war. That was a quote from your original Limaj testimony which you adopted in court yesterday. I want to ask you, sir, if -- if I'm understanding you correctly. Is that your testimony that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: -- that no collaborator --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, I take it it was paragraph 69 of the -- of the investigator's notes. Is that correct or were you referring to the Limaj --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: This is to the Limaj transcript, Your Honour, this is the same page we were just dealing with, 5066.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to be clear Mr. Kearney is in error. It wasn't dealt with in the Limaj transcript that passage, it was dealt with in the transcript yesterday at 5066, and it's a reference to the investigator's note, so he's not putting a passage from the Limaj transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I stand corrected in that regard, Your Honour, and I'll re-pose the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Paragraph 69, then talking about. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, you testified yesterday you adopted a statement you made in your interview notes. I'm just going to quote the sentence again. You additionally stressed that to your knowledge no collaborators were arrested or executed by the KLA during the war. Sir, do you have that answer that you gave yesterday in mind?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry -- I'm sorry to keep rising but it is important to get this right. Mr. Kearney has just put to the witness that the answer he gave was that no collaborators was arrested or executed. Now, just to be clear, we know what the passage says, it says arrested and executed; in other words, as the following sentence makes clear, if people died, it was not following arrest. Now, the way the question has been put implies that the witness said in his interview, for example, and separately, that no collaborator had ever been arrested. So if the matter is to be put, it should be put accurately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I -- Mr. Emmerson, I agree with you that sometimes it could be more precise; at the same time, the -- where it's not for the full hundred per cent precise, that creates no confusion here I would say. Mr. Kearney, would you please try to be as precise as possible, preferably quoting literally and in context whatever you put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'd be happy to read the line literally, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, once again, this is a statement from your interview to the OTP that was talked about yesterday, specifically paragraph 69. In that statement it was written: "He additionally stressed that to his knowledge no collaborators were arrested and executed." Do you remember being questioned about that yesterday in court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, I asked you to put it in the context, and context yesterday, the quote put to Mr. Krasniqi, but I'll now put it to him. Yesterday it was put to you that you gave a statement and the statement read as follows: "Mr. Krasniqi stated that the General Staff stressed frequently that the KLA must obey and respect the international norms and not target civilians. He additionally stressed that to his knowledge no collaborators were arrested and executed. Some may have been killed, but that would have happened during battle at the front line, never after detention." Put the question you would like to put to the witness, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Is it your testimony, Mr. Krasniqi, that the KLA during the war never arrested and executed a single collaborator?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Are you aware of any arrests of collaborators by the KLA during the war?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term that is being used very often here, "collaborationist," is not the proper term to be used for every case. Although it was not within the sphere of my responsibility, I know of people who were stopped and then released. I know of a case of two Albanians who were stopped and then released. I don't know anything further than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: These two Albanians who were stopped and released, were they suspected collaborationists?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were suspected to have conducted propaganda against the war. Maybe that's why they were stopped and then they were released.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, by your own definition of collaborator that you gave yesterday, I would presume that you would not characterise that activity of giving propaganda against the war as collaboration; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's why they were treated the way they were treated. They were released. Every time you stop someone could not have been treated as collaborating.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, please listen to my question. You just indicated that there -- you were aware of only two Albanians who were stopped and then released -- or you gave us that example earlier in your questioning. You said the reason they were stopped is because they had conducted propaganda against the war. I want to ask you, sir, if based on the definition you gave to this Tribunal yesterday of what collaboration is you would characterise as giving propaganda against the war as collaboration.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To be against the war does not mean that you are a collaborationist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: So, sir, those two Albanians that you just mentioned were, by your own definition, not collaborators. Are you -- beyond those two arrested Albanians who were released, are you aware of no other suspected collaborators who were arrested by the KLA during the war?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, in communiques issued --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Because we're dealing with such a sensitive issue, the question last asked by Mr. Kearney is a mis -- is a potential misstatement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- of the testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you say is those arrested Albanians were in the testimony of the witness not qualified as collaborators, that's, I think, is clear. Mr. Kearney, I take it that you, when you said, "beyond those two arrested Albanians" of other suspected collaborators that you certainly you were aware that Mr. Krasniqi had testified that these persons were not collaborators.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Certainly. And the reason I included those was they were the answer that this witness gave to my initial question about collaborators. But I think his answer now is clear, Your Honour. I'm prepared to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you do so I would like to have one thing straight. Earlier you were asked whether you knew, and I'll literally quote -- you were asked: "Is it your testimony, Mr. Krasniqi, that the KLA during the war never arrested and executed a single collaborator?" Your answer was: "That's what I said." I want you to be fully aware that there is a difference between a positive statement that the KLA during the war never arrested and executed a single collaborator and - and that's different - whether you know about the KLA ever arresting and executing a collaborator during the war. So we should clearly distinguish between whether you have positive knowledge that it never happened or that you do not know about that it ever happened. Now, which of the two, because in the last question you were asked about your knowledge. Can you say for sure that the KLA never arrested and executed a single collaborator? Or is your testimony that you do not know of any case of the KLA arresting and executing a collaborator? Which of the two is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My answer is the following. I do not know of any case during that period of a collaborationist, Albanians collaborating with the Serbs, being detained and subsequently killed. So my answer refers to my knowledge. I do not know of such cases and I have not heard of such cases. This would be my specific answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kearney, you'll understand that this sheds a certain light on the testimony I just quoted, that is, page 28, line 17. Now, the next question: Did you ever hear of an arrest of a collaborator without subsequential or subsequent killing of that person by the KLA? So that is being detained for some time and then being released again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I did not hear about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you ever hear about a collaborator being executed by the KLA without previously being arrested and/or detained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We've heard about this through the communiques.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means the KLA executing - and under executing, I understand killing someone in this context for the reason that he had collaborated and not just because he was at the front line as a soldier but specifically aiming at that person because of his collaboration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will repeat myself yet again: My knowledge never leave a space for me to understand or believe that the KLA, having detained a collaborationist, subsequently killed him or her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But my last question was about killing the collaborationist without arresting and detaining him, whether you know of any such a case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What we know is from the communiques released in the name of the KLA General Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if the witness might remove his headphones at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please take your headphones of for a second, Mr. Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm entirely in Your Honour's hands as to how far this matter needs to be pursued at this stage. Obviously the use of the word "execution" in the context of somebody who has not been detained leaves open a number of possibilities about the circumstances. For example, whether the target was armed or unarmed at the time; whether they're properly to be classified as a combatant or noncombatant. These are issues about which very detailed factual examination would be required of the circumstances of the particular individuals concerned. And I think the position of this witness is that he's not able to give detailed information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, my exercise was mainly aiming at seeking --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to better understand what he testified and not going into every detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not complaining at all about Your Honour's questions. I'm simply raising the fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I'm aware that an execution could take all kind of different forms and could be done under all kind of different circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Or against a person who's armed at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not saying that -- I mean, if someone at his door-step with an arm in his hands is killed by those - I just give an example, not from this case - but by those who have rang at the door then, of course, he could be armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just noticed that whenever Your Honour used the word "execution" in the question, the witness would respond with the word "killing", as it came through in the translation. And it simply may be that with this witness not knowing anything about the circumstances of the incidents described, it's simply impossible to get to the bottom of whether or not which side of the line a particular incident falls.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the reason I stopped when the witness referred to the communiques as a source of knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I have one moment to confer with my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, speaking of those communiques you just referred to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Your headphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, speaking of those communiques we just referred to, in 1997, the communiques - these are -- I'm referring to annex 1, 2, 4, and 5, that's Exhibit 386 - those communiques issued by the General Staff list name, village, and date of several collaborators being killed. Is that correct? And I'm -- I'll say their names now. Hetem Dobruna in Lozice village in May 1997; Ali Qullapeku, Q-u-l-l-a-p-e-k-u, from Terstenik; Ramiz Leku from Glogovac; Qamil Gashi on 18 November, also from Glogovac; Dalip Dugolli on 28 November from Petreshice. Are you familiar with those names, sir, having read them in the communiques?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned about these names from the communiques as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And I want to ask you a follow-up question. Based on your experience, your long tenure with the KLA during the decade of the 1990s, do you have any reason to doubt that information that was published in General Staff communiques regarding those collaborators?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I object to the question. No foundation laid. Quite clear the witness doesn't know the basis of the information. A question which seeks by negative to elicit the fact that the material the witness is not aware of in contradiction is another way to ask the witness to affirm that which he's not in a position to affirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: These are communiques issued by his own General Staff, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm -- the question was whether, based on the experience of the witness, he had -- there were a few circumstances specifically mentioned, Mr. Kearney, which suggest that they would put the witness in a better position to doubt or not doubt that matter. Now, however you are -- you are allowed whether the witness ever learned of any circumstance that would make him doubt about whether the content of the communiques was correct or not -- or was incorrect, as a matter of fact. Is there anything you ever learned which would make you believe that the information contained in the communiques you just mentioned, specifically in relation to the events mentioned in the question by Mr. Kearney, was there ever anything you learned that created doubt in your mind as to whether this was perhaps not correct information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the issue of 1997 has been already covered on several occasions by me. For the cases mentioned earlier, I learned about them from the communiques. The communiques at that time were part of the operational department, and I really didn't have any knowledge about those communiques and about these actions of the operational department during 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, the question was whether you ever learned, not necessarily from the communiques, but from whatever source any -- learn anything that created doubt as to the correctness of these communiques in your mind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Simply, I didn't deal with this issue. It was not my area of responsibility. I dealt with totally different issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understand the answer then to be that you never learned any circumstance that -- that you didn't pay, perhaps, much attention to these matters but -- because it was not in your responsibility, but you can't say, I, at that time, learned this and this and this which made me doubt whether it was correct what the communique said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot say anything about this because I didn't deal with this issue, as I said. I can't give you any affirmative answer to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm informed by my colleague that the books that we have been waiting for relating to this witness have just arrived. I wonder if the Court would consider taking a break five, ten minutes earlier at this time so we can disseminate these to counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that mean that you have no further questions in re-examination or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: No, I do have approximately 15 more minutes for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If the suggestion is that somehow this witness's testimony will start all over again once we've had an opportunity to assimilate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not anticipate on the situation after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Obviously we'd be grateful to receive it but nobody's going to be in a position to assimilate this material whilst this witness is still being examined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unless the books are very thin. Therefore I said let's not anticipate on what's going to happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have an early break. We'll resume at five minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, I suggest to you and to the Defence that I do not ask at this moment one single question about whether there is a book, how many books there are, just let's first continue the examination of the witness as matters stand -- stood until -- even if you don't ask for matters, sometimes -- well, three, as a matter of fact. I'll put them upside down. I suggest that we first finish the examination -- the re-examination of the witness. Mr. Kearney, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, I have just a couple more questions about the communiques and then I'll move on. You mentioned during your cross-examination by Mr. Emmerson that the communiques that were written in 1997 were authored by members of the diaspora, specifically in, I believe, Switzerland and Albania. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it was possible that they were the authors, but who the authors were, indeed, that I don't know. It is possible that those communiques were written or authored by members of the General Staff that were in Albania or in Switzerland, but to what extent that is true, that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I just want to ask you a question. I'm looking at page 5026 of your transcript, lines 6 and 7. You gave an answer saying -- and just to give you a grounding, I'll read the question as well at line 3. "Q. And would it be fair to say that you did not know the names of more than half or less than half of the other members of the body calling itself the General Staff?" Your answer: "Well, it's difficult to say now because I know all of them now, but at the time I did not know some of them." My question is: Do you now know the remainder of the General Staff who was -- you referred to earlier as part of the diaspora in Switzerland and Albania?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, now I know all of them. Eight years have passed since the war happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And who were the members of the General Staff that were living in the diaspora back in 1997, please?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Azem Syla, Xhavit Haliti, Bardhyl Mahmuti, Ali Ahmeti, Kadri Veseli, they were in the diaspora.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I assume you've talked to those men since 1997. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean after 1997? Well, even during the war some of them were not in Kosova. With some of them, I met after 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Based on your contact with them since 1997, have you learned who authored the communiques from 1997 that are attached to your statement?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You were asked by Mr. Emmerson about annex 2 to your statement. This is communique 35 published on 8 August 1997 in Koha Ditore. In that communique you were asked specifically about guerilla operations carried out against Serb policemen and two Albanian civilians as well as three armed authorisations -- operations, excuse me, that were authorised by the General Staff on the 3rd and 4th of August, 1997. You were asked by Mr. Emmerson if you knew of these operations in 1997. Your answer was: "No." But then you gave the following answer, this is at page 5041: "At the time I had no knowledge about these operations. I may know of them, today" and this is at the very end of 5041, continuing on to 5042. "At the time I had no knowledge about these operations. I may know of them today, but not at that time." I want to ask you: What do you know about these operations, if anything, at this time that you did not know back in 1997?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which operations are you referring to because there are many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes. I'm referring to the ones that you told us you have information or you may have information about now that you didn't back in 1997?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, just so that there's no misunderstanding might the witness be directed to the specific annex communique that I was asking him questions about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's annex 2 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly. And to the lines and the particular operations that were there being referred to so that he knows exactly what it is he is being asked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Is the blue folder with the annexes in Albanian still available for this witness, Madam Usher?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it then please be provided to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which number did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Number 2, and this is -- the beginning of the first full paragraph is what I'll be questioning you on, Mr. Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's only in one portion that operations are -- I think three operations are mentioned, Mr. Kearney. If you would specifically draw the attention of the witness to those.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, do you see the second full sentence in the text which starts: "This communique states ..." Do you see that -- those words, sir? I'll read the sentence for you to see if you can find it. "This communique states: 'By a decision of the UCK Central Staff made on 3 and 4 August our guerilla units carried out three armed operations against the occupiers and their collaborators.'" Do you see that statement?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, no -- yes, now I do, on 3rd and 4th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, yesterday during your testimony you were asked by Mr. Emmerson about the operations that are referenced in that annex and you said: "At the time I did not have any knowledge about those operations. I may know of them today but not at the time." Can you please tell us, Mr. Krasniqi, what you know, if anything, about those operations now that you did not know in 1997, please.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wrote a book, "The Big Turn," and in order to write that book I had to consult some literature. And while consulting that literature, I learned about these operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And can you please tell us more specifically about these operations. Which operations are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned about this one that you read in the communique.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And what did you learn about those operations, please?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing in addition to what is here in the communique.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Did you learn that in August of 1997 there were, in fact, three operations conducted on the orders of the UCK Central Staff?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the communique, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: But, Mr. Krasniqi, you just told us that in writing your book, "The Big Turn" you consulted literature about these operations. What literature did you consult?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The communiques.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to get to the core of the issue. You say that you learned about the operations, whereas you had no knowledge of what they were in 1997. What were these operations, three operations? Against what? What type of operation? The Chamber's got no idea about what we are talking about, so could you tell us. Let's start with the first. First operation would be where? What? If you know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know anything else. All I know is what the communique says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I then understand that whereas in 1997 you were not aware of these operations, that you later by consulting the communiques learned that there had been three operations but that you do not know anything additional to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: In your book, Mr. Krasniqi, "The Big Turn," do you describe any of the operations that were conducted by the KLA during 1997?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my book I mainly deal with political issues, organisational issues. I also treat of the KLA from the time it was formed. I write about the legendary commander Adem Jashari and his family. I give information about political developments --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I speak about some fightings, but not specific operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You started giving us the full content of the book, more or less, whereas the specific question was whether operations were described. If at any later stage, I don't know whether we are going to do that or not, if at any later stage, we would read this book of yours or any other book you may have written, would we find further details about operations, early August 1997, by KLA units, such as where the operations took place --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, you wouldn't. There isn't such information there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: In your book, do you describe the fact --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. I've allowed this line of questioning to go on, but we don't have the books in a form in which we can understand them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They haven't been raised in cross-examination. None of these questions arise out of cross-examination and it is not fair or proper for Mr. Kearney to conduct re-examination on the content of books that haven't been disclosed or analysed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, joining I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, and we had an agreement there would be no discussion about the books other than they were, in fact, books of Mr. Krasniqi's.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, I take it that you join as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: It would be very surprising if I didn't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me then just for the record say that I see on my desk three books, one apparently written in a language I could read; two in a language which I'm not familiar with. Mr. Kearney, do you have knowledge of the content of the book -- of one of these books?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I don't, and I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'm just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, you are -- in your questions you are asking -- I asked the witness if I would read that book would we find any further information about this. There might be a stage that the Chamber would read that book if one of the parties, after having read it, tenders it and if there's no objections. But at this moment you're alluding to what you would expect to be in the book, whereas the witness, of course, as far as early August 1997 operations is concerned, the witness denied that we'll find anything in the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Chamber's point is well-taken. The reason I pursued this line of questioning was because this witness himself said that he learned during his apparent research for the book or writing of the book of some of the operations in question; that's what I was pursuing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I asked him specifically then how to understand that. And what the witness then said is that whereas he may not have been aware of the operations, perhaps because he had not seen the communiques at that time, that later on when he consulted the communiques that he learned that there were three operations without any further details. I think that was the clear testimony of the witness. Then I asked him whether we would find anything else in the book, which of course gives an opportunity to the parties to check the credibility and reliability of those answers. So please proceed and I do understand that there's an agreement between the parties that the content of the book as such is not subject of examining of the witness at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I just have one last question in this area and then I'm going to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, do you have knowledge of guerilla operations taking place by the KLA in 1997 at all?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ones that we mentioned several times so far and that you find in the communiques.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, you also mentioned in your cross-examination that there was a point in time when you learned that Ramush Haradinaj was the -- had a commanding role in the Dukagjin Zone. I'm going to read you a question and answer by way of foundation on page 5051 at line 11. You were asked by Mr. Emmerson: "And was that the first occasion on which you became aware that he had any commanding role in the Dukagjin area?" And perhaps I should back up a question. At line 7: "Can I ask you please, first of all, is it correct then that the first time you met Mr. Haradinaj was at the end of June/beginning of July, that was the first occasion you'd met?" Your answer was: "Yes." The next question was: "And was that the first occasion on which you became aware that he had any commanding role in the Dukagjini area?" Your answer was: "No, I knew this from before, before I went." And finally, the last question I seek to discuss with you is: "Q. I see. Would it coincide with his appoint -- appointment on the 23rd of June approximately?" Your answer was: "Yes." Mr. Krasniqi, do you remember those questions and those answers given by you yesterday?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember them very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Do you remember in your Limaj testimony being asked a similar question, this is at transcript page 3480, beginning at line 1. First of all, do you remember being asked questions on this same topic about during what period Mr. Haradinaj was a commander of the Dukagjin Zone?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Limaj case I was not asked questions about Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Let me see, Mr. Krasniqi, if this refreshes your memory in that regard, starting at page 1. "Q. Same thing, yes. Who was the commander of that zone as you recall it, again in this period of time April to August, if you can help by remembering? "A. The zone commander he was such later, but at this period it was Ramush Haradinaj." Do you remember giving that answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe I've mentioned April. I must have said later, when he was appointed. When I was appointed as spokesperson after the 23rd of June, not about April. I didn't say anything about April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, did Mr. Haradinaj have de facto command of the Dukagjin Zone before he was formally appointed in June of 1997?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I believe you're asking for legal conclusion at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, if you would reformulate your question, which of course asks for an assessment of -- a qualification, as a matter of fact, of a certain situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The answer that the witness gave in the Limaj case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we see the answer. Limaj, of course, is -- transcript is in evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So Your Honour's seen the answer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I wouldn't say it makes matters much clearer --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's my point.
