utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's as a matter of fact is commenting both on question and answer given by the witness at this moment. But, Mr. Kearney, perhaps you ask the witness what he could tell us about the position of Mr. Haradinaj and then further develop what you seem to seek.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Isn't it true, Mr. Krasniqi, based on your answer in Limaj that in fact, not pursuant to appointment by the General Staff, but in fact, Ramush Haradinaj --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I object to the form of the question. It's a leading question based on an ambiguous answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, you should, if you ask -- if you refer to the answer given by the witness at that time after such a period of time, then you should at least put the answer he gave at that time and then you can ask further questions. And I think, as a matter of fact -- no, it has been -- let me just see. You have read to him the answer. You asked the witness whether he remembered that he gave that answer, and then he says: "I don't believe I mentioned April." So there's a challenge as to the transcript reflects what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: With respect, first of all he didn't mention a month at all in his answer. He was asked a question and he gives an answer which, as I sought to emphasise a moment ago --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, excuse me. If we're going to be having a conversation about this, may we have the witness take off his earphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm very happy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Take off your earphones, Mr. Krasniqi. We can all read. Let's refer to the lines we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes -- what was occurring --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think at page 46, line 22, Mr. Kearney said he would refresh the memory of the witness. Then he read to him the question. The question relates to a period April to August in Limaj, and then the witness answered: "The zone commander he was such later, but at this period it was Ramush Haradinaj."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which -- and then the witness was asked whether he gave that answer. He said then: "I don't believe I've mentioned April." That seems to be correct on the basis of the transcript, because the question mentioned April and he referred to a later period and he also said that at this period --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it was Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just develop my concern about this, just for a moment. At that point in his cross-examination in the Limaj case, Mr. Mansfield for Mr. Limaj was running through each of the zones at something of a trot, asking for a brief picture, a snap-shot. He put the question to the witness in relation to all zones for the period that he was concerned with, and the witness replies: "The zone commander he was such later but at this period it was Ramush Haradinaj." Now, "this period" could mean a period earlier, it could mean April to August, or it could mean the period he refers to when he says, "he was such later"; in other words, "The zone commander he was such later at this period" - i.e., later when he was zone commander - "it was Ramush Haradinaj." Now, no attempt was made in Limaj because it wasn't necessary to seek to elicit clarification. If Mr. Kearney wishes to put to this witness the question and answer that he gave and ask him whether that is, in his view, consistent with his testimony in a nonleading form then I have no objection. My objection is to the question asked just a moment ago, page 48, line 6, on the basis of which Mr. Kearney seeks to elicit a meaning from that answer and put it in a leading form to the witness. And my objections are two-fold. He's not entitled to put leading questions in re-examination, and he's certainly not entitled to put leading questions on the basis of a selective understanding from the Prosecution of an ambiguous answer from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, would you agree that the answer in Limaj is quite ambiguous?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: No, I think this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please tell me how I -- I mean, the witness has now his earphones off. Mr. Emmerson tells us that it's an ambiguous answer and you tell us it's not. How do we have to understand the answer in your view.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the answer is very clear. He's asked about a period, April to August. This is a -- I would remind the Trial Chamber this is an educated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And before the witness puts his earphones back on, the word "de facto" that I used that was objected to by Mr. Guy-Smith, this is a word this witness used himself in his interview notes. I don't think it calls for a legal conclusion. With the Trial Chamber's permission I would like to use that word again in forming the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, as a matter of fact, if you then could do that -- as a matter of fact, I asked you about the ambiguity of the answer on page 3480, line 4 and 5, but you didn't address that matter. If you want to ask the witness about these matters, the Chamber would prefer you not to do it on the basis of the answer he gave in Limaj. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, was there a period before Mr. Haradinaj was appointed formally zone commander that he was the de facto commander of that zone?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could say he was or he wasn't. I think this was a prejudiced question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Officially he was made commander on the 23rd of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, what Mr. Kearney is asking you, whether Mr. Haradinaj, before he was officially appointed commander, exercised de facto command which, let's try to keep matters simple, means that he gave instructions and orders to KLA members, units - whatever you know about this, tell us - in that period of time. Mr. Emmerson, I'd like first --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes -- [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'd first have the witness answer the question rather than giving his opinion about the answer -- about the question. Could you tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before he was appointed commander, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, I want to ask you questions now about Mr. Brahimaj, following-up or seeking some clarifications about questions put to you by Mr. Harvey yesterday. You told us about after 11 June 1998 you began to work with Mr. Brahimaj in the General Staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You told us a great deal about geographically where these meetings took place. I want to ask you now in June of 1998 about time, not geography but time. Tell us, please, in the remainder of June 1998 after the 11th of June, how often did the General Staff meet?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to give you an accurate number of those meetings. Maybe we met two or three times, maybe more, but I can't give you an exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: That would be two to three times in the remainder of June 1998; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it's difficult for me now to give you an accurate number, two times, three times. It was difficult for us to move at that time. The situation was very difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: These meetings that you're describing, how long would they last typically?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on the issues that we had to discuss or to have a joint stand about. It could be two hours or three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, after June, in July, is it true from -- is my understanding true from your testimony yesterday that the frequency of these meetings decreased as the summer offensives began?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. The offensives hindered us from moving, and it was not possible for us to meet more often.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Can you give us any estimate, Mr. Krasniqi, of how often in July then the General Staff met?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say. Once or twice, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you the same question about August, please. How many times -- and I realise this is a long time ago, but could you tell us how many times did the General Staff meet in August of 1998?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember because August was the month when the Serb offensive had reached its climax and I don't know whether we had an opportunity to meet even once or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: So these meetings that happened in June, July, and August that you just described, did Mr. Brahimaj attend all of these meetings or were there some that he missed?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's been a long time, of course, and it's difficult for me to give you an accurate answer. But sometimes, because of the distance from the Dukagjini Zone, Lahi Brahimaj could not move in those areas. Maybe he crossed the boundaries illegally to come from one area to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: So are you saying that because of the distance from the Dukagjini Zone there was some meetings that Mr. Brahimaj did not attend or did he attend all of the meetings? I'm not clear on your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you an accurate answer regarding the number of meetings that he did attend and did not attend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, the first question was whether he missed some. Without asking for numbers, was he always present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, I was not dealing with this matter, who attended and who didn't. That's why it's difficult for me to pinpoint whether he missed a meeting or not. But bearing in mind the fact that the fighting was quite intensive during this time, the possibility for a member of the General Staff to be absent from a meeting was quite there, although Lahi Brahimaj was quite disciplined about these meetings. He was almost in every one of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that's finally the answer, then, is that he often attended but you cannot be sure whether he always attended, which is understandable for you due to the circumstances at the time. Is that correct understanding of your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You mentioned the distance of the Dukagjini Zone from the -- the area of the General Staff meetings in Negrovce, Klecka, Divjake. What was that distance?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, we have maps. Let's not ask witnesses about distances if we can look at it. If it has any specific relevance, then please ask for the relevant -- but let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: In fact, Your Honour, I do have a map of this. It's marked as 65 ter 1351 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: -- perhaps we could bring it up at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But so then we can see what the distance is? Please proceed. Do you want to tender the map, Mr. Kearney?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P329, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, just for the Court's and the Trial Chamber's clarification, the blue square lines on this map represent 10 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, can you see this map?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Does that fit with your knowledge, sir, of the geography of Kosovo; namely, the distance from Jabllanice there on the map to your home village as well as the other villages that you mentioned in your testimony yesterday?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, how long does it take to drive from Jabllanice to your home village in Negrovce?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean how long would it take today or during the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Tell us both, please.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Today it's, of course, much faster, within 40 minutes, because the road is not straight, it goes up; while during war the distance was not that big but the difficulties were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: In June of 1998, how long in your experience -- you were living there at the time, how long would it have taken to drive from your village to Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was twice, during the war, travelled from Divjake to Jabllanice, and it took me a long time for this journey because we had to walk for one part of the road and then get to the asphalt road Klina-Gjakove, which was at the time controlled by the police and military Serb forces. So before reaching Jabllanice we had to cross the Drini River, and from the villages of Malisheve municipality, Llapsheve and up to Jabllanice we had to travel on foot and that took us several hours and we mainly travelled at night-time for security reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: So is it your testimony that the -- in June of 1998 this trip from Jabllanice, say from Divjake would have taken several hours?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, how long did you work with Mr. Brahimaj after June of 1998? How long did you consider him a colleague of yours in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the entire time. He's still a colleague of ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: When you say "still," are you talking about this year, 2007?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the period after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: During this period of time that you worked with Mr. Brahimaj, did you consider him a friend, sir?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Is that still the case, Mr. Krasniqi? Do you consider Mr. Brahimaj a friend even today?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do. Nothing has changed between us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you the same question regarding Mr. Haradinaj. Do you still consider him or do you consider him a friend today as you sit here in court?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Haradinaj was a comrade in arms. He was a good fighter and I have respect for him even today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Lastly, I want to talk to you about Mr. Balaj. Is this a person that you met during the war as well?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't meet him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, I want to return to your last answer. In response to my question regarding Mr. Haradinaj if he was a friend, you said: "He was a comrade in arms. He was a good fighter and I have respect for him even today." My question is more simple than that: Is he a friend of yours today?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of fact you did not, but I understood your answer to be the following, that you're not personal friends, but nevertheless that you, due to his past, you respect him very much, which is not exactly the same as personal friendship. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know how to understand "personal friendship." We didn't have a personal friendship, but a joint cause made us be comrade in arms, co-fighters, and have the same goal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: But since the war, Mr. Krasniqi, in the government in Kosovo have you worked with Mr. Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: You indicated that you did not meet Mr. Balaj during the war. Have you met him since the war?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, without telling us the contents, have you ever given a statement to the Defence during the investigation of this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's a question that could have been addressed to me. I'd like to know the relevance and how it arises out of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'm trying to explore this witness's bias, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I'm perfectly prepared to answer the question and I'll do it in a proper form, but it should have been asked to me if Mr. Kearney wanted to do it. He's not in a position to explore bias of his own witness in re-examination. It's not a proper way to conduct a re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, certainly it's not a question that arises out of cross-examination, but I understand that Mr. Emmerson is willing to give you the information. If there's any reason then for follow-up questions, we'll hear them and see how to -- whether there will be any objections against it. Mr. Emmerson, are you willing to give the information?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm happy to communicate that as far as I'm aware, we have never, nobody on our team has ever interviewed this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask whether that would be true for all of the Defence teams.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Never had any contact with Mr. Krasniqi before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, if there's any need to put further questions in relation to this, we'll hear them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: There's not, Your Honour, and in case of fact, I have no more questions of this witness. We do have some administrative matters to discuss, namely the books and the 92 ter summaries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would first of all like to give an opportunity to Defence counsel whether there's any need for re-examination. Yes, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, there is one matter that arises out of the fresh questions put by Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I said re-examination but of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Re-cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, re-cross. Yes, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry to Mr. Harvey but just regarding the books we are going to need just to ask - maybe the Chambers can do it - just ask him in point of fact what these books are, if he wrote them, just a basic foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey. Further cross-examination by Mr. Harvey:

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, you were asked a few questions ago by Mr. Kearney concerning your opportunities to meet with Lahi Brahimaj at meetings of the General Staff. He did not ask you whether you met with him outside meetings of the General Staff, so I'd just like to come to that point with you for a moment. Aside from meetings of the General Staff, while you were stationed in Drenica, did you meet with Lahi Brahimaj during the month of June?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Again, I appreciate what you said about it being difficult to remember the frequency of such meetings, but would you be able to assist the Tribunal to any extent in indicating how frequent your contacts were with him in Drenica during the month of June outside General Staff meetings?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember how frequent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Would you say more than once? More than twice? Or are you simply unable to recall at this stage?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you the accurate number, but we did meet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Same question for the month of July.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And I assume I would get the same answer in August and September?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: August and September were quite difficult months for meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Hoepfel has one or more questions for you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krasniqi, may I also take you back to these meetings of the General Staff in mid-1998. Now, yesterday and today you gave us already some explanations. There were -- such as where these meetings took place. And you were asked as to the meeting on the 23rd of June, 1998, when Mr. Ramush Haradinaj, as you said, "officially was made commander"; i.e., commander of the Dukagjini Zone. So I'd like to ask you about the way this election or appointment was conducted. First, would you call this an election or appointment?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an appointment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Further, how was this decision taken? You were present, I assume; is this right?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And how many else were present?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe it will be difficult for me to tell you how many there were present because quite a long time has passed, but we were seven, approximately, because not all attended that meeting. We had quite a long discussion, and in the end we adopted the decision to appoint the commanders of the Drenica, Pashtrik, and Dukagjini Zones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- although it's not very usual to interrupt if a Judge puts questions to a witness but if there's anything, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I do apologise for interrupting. I just wanted to make sure that there wasn't any confusion here between the meeting on the 23rd of June which took place in Lapusnik at which, to the best of my knowledge and belief, Mr. Krasniqi was not present, and a subsequent meeting of the General Staff that would have taken place to ratify the appointment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We're now having multiple interruptions in the Judge's questions. I think Mr. Harvey must not have meant to say, "Lapusnik."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Absolutely right, I'm sorry. I'm having a flashback. Jabllanice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes. Can you help us. So were you present at the meeting where this appointment was decided or was this already --

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring to an appointment in Jabllanice, that I don't know. As far as the appointment made in Divjake, this I know and what I told you refers to this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And as far as you know, was the will of those members of the General Staff who were absent taken into some account? I will be more specific. First, as you were not present, were you asked before about the decision to be taken then in this meeting?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I was present at the meeting in Klecke when the commander of the Dukagjin Zone was appointed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes. And do you know how, if any, expressions of the will of those absent were factored in?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not my duty to deal with this issue. This was somebody else's responsibility as far as others were concerned, but the appointment of Mr. Haradinaj as a commander of the Dukagjini Zone was done pursuant to the will of the majority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. There are some questions arising out of that line of questioning, if Your Honour would permit me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I would first like to finish the questions of the Judge --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry I thought Judge Hoepfel --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I am done but maybe there are other questions of the Bench and you will have an opportunity later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, during your examination, questions were put to you in relation to a paragraph found in the investigator's notes which relate to the May 2004 interview. I read the whole of the paragraph to you. Paragraph 81: "When asked if the commander of an operational zone would know what was happening in his area of responsibility, Mr. Krasniqi stated that they did, in fact, try to know but this at times proved difficult. Commanders, however, were obliged to inform the General Staff of any crimes or breaches committed, and the General Staff would then order appropriate action." What would be the appropriate action to be ordered when information about crimes or breaches would have been received?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The General Staff and the KLA did not have, first of all, did not have a higher body, such as an assembly or parliament that would make the laws. It was more on -- based on the will and the readiness of the individuals to take upon themselves responsibilities in the interest of the nation, but what would these responsibilities would be in case a commander of a zone or another person informed of illegal acts or breaches of laws on war, these measures would be the following: The person would be known who committed that crime or breach; then the measures that would follow would be the ones removing him from the position where he was. At that time the General Staff and the KLA did not have the proper mechanisms to take any other measures, just to publicly remove those ones from positions, those ones who would commit crimes or breaches. The General Staff publicly distanced themselves from the actions in the terrain that were not supported by the members of the General Staff and that were far from the policy pursued by the General Staff. If necessary, I can mention two cases in relation to which the General Staff of the KLA publicly reacted. One of the cases occurred in Drenica when one -- somebody from the ranks of the KLA stopped a truck and this truck was driven by a Serb national. This truck was stopped. We interfered and we released the driver and his truck. And we told them that this stop was carried out by irresponsible people and that these irresponsible people are not allowed to carry out such actions. So this is one of the cases when the General Staff interfered. The second case is when a hand-grenade was thrown in Peje, in a cafeteria in Peje which was full of Serbian youth. There were casualties, injured, and in this case the General Staff publicly distanced itself from such violations and attacks on unarmed civilians. So what we proclaimed in our statements that we're waging a war against the apparatus and against the Serbian regime but not against the citizens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. I'd like to refer to part of your testimony of today which was against two persons who had conducted propaganda against the war. You told us that that may have been the reason why they were stopped and, as you said, then they were released. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You also told us that -- as a matter of fact, you were asked then, whether by your own definition of collaborator, whether it is correct that you would not characterise the activity of giving propaganda against the war as being collaboration. And you confirmed that it was correct. Then you said the following: "That's why they were treated the way they were treated. They were released. Every time you stop someone could not have been treated as collaborating." In your answer there is a suggestion that being released is because they were not collaborators; is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would also suggest that if you would stop collaborators, that you would not release them.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please explain to me. Is it that you wouldn't stop collaborators or you would also release them. Then it becomes not quite understandable for me how you made that distinction. Could you please explain how I should understand it in any other way as I did put it to you.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KLA did not have the means and the possibility to have prisons and to detain collaborationists. Because, first of all, they were protected by the Serb forces and collaborators were called those people or those Albanians who worked in the Serb secret police or otherwise called Serb intelligence service. I'd like to make a clarification here. The Serb intelligence service is not the same as Western intelligence services which collect information and then leave the relevant bodies deal with them. The Serb service was an executive body as well, and they executed decisions on the basis of the information they got. And these people who were collaborators of the Serbs, of course they did not move around in the war areas and it wasn't possible for us to detain or imprison them. We didn't have any prisons, but maybe there were points, crossing points, where people who looked suspicious were stopped. But even this was limited. I repeat, the KLA did not have the possibilities to have any prisons or detain people because the area was also limited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I want to be quite frank with you. It's -- still does not explain clearly your testimony, whereas you said you release them every time you stop someone could not have been treated as collaborating. That's what you said and your answer does not fully explain. I just put it to you so that if you want to add anything to your explanation that you have an opportunity to do so. You answered my question, but I just want to be frank with you that it not in every respect makes me fully understand the distinction you made earlier in your answer between the release of two persons not being collaborators.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, I wouldn't mind calling them collaborators. I don't know whether to call them or not. They were against the war. They conducted propaganda against the war, but I can't call them collaborators. Collaborators to us were those people who collaborated and who worked for the Serb regime and the Serb police and army but not somebody who refused to enter a war. A collaborator was somebody who was part of the mechanism, who was part of the apparatus and served that apparatus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me try to make it as clear to you as I can. In your answer there's a clear suggestion, and I think you confirmed that, that there is a distinction between the way you treat collaborators and these two people you considered not to be collaborators. The not collaborators, of which you now say you could call them also collaborators but you wouldn't do it, the -- at least these two persons were released, which leaves the question open what one would do if those who were stopped were collaborators. That's not entirely clear to me at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the answer. Could the witness repeat it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the answer because the interpreters couldn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did not stop collaborators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Mr. Emmerson, you had --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- some more questions triggered by the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Principally arising out of Judge Hoepfel's questions. Might I just ask the witness to remove his headphones for one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krasniqi, could you please remove your headphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It may be that Your Honour's taken that last line of questioning as far as it needs to be taken. There's simply one matter that struck me as Your Honour was asking the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's in relation to the last of the three sentences in the passage that Your Honour quoted to the witness which most recently I think appears at page 66, line 23. The first two sentences read: "That's why they were treated the way they were treated. They were released," sorry, page 65, line 23. Then and then there is a sentence that reads: "Every time you stopped someone could not have been treated as collaborating." On the face of it that is a sentence with a grammatical difficulty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understand the -- yes. If you would take it grammatically purely then --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It wouldn't -- yes. I mean, the only reason I mention it is simply to see whether Your Honour wants to take it any further or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that -- it struck me that what that might be is a rough translation of -- or an approximate translation of the mere fact that someone has been stopped --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I will do, Mr. Emmerson, is to ask the specific attention of those who are transcribing and those who are translating and to check on the basis of the original words spoken by the witness whether there is a grammatical difficulty or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't think it of great use at this moment to further pursue the matter. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if the witness could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please put your earphones on again, Mr. Krasniqi. Further cross-examination by Mr. Emmerson:

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, just for the sake of clarification, Judge Hoepfel asks you some questions, this is the Judge who sits to your left in front of you, asked you some questions about the -- a meeting at which the General Staff took a decision about the appointment of a commander for the Dukagjini region and specifically he asked you whether you understood it to be an appointment or an election. Now, in this case we have seen detailed minutes recording a meeting on the 23rd of June that took place in Jabllanice at which there was a lengthy -- or there is recorded a lengthy discussion which culminates in a decision to create a staff for the Dukagjini Plain Operational Zone, and is followed by what appears to be an election with Ramush Haradinaj being nominated by one party and Lahi Brahimaj being nominated by another. And then speeches taking place in favour of one or the other and culminating in a vote by a majority in favour of Ramush Haradinaj as zone commander. Now, that is a meeting which you were not present at, is that not correct? You were not there at that meeting in Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was not present in Jabllanice. If you are referring to a Jabllanice meeting, I don't know about that, and that was not a meeting of the General Staff. Maybe it was a meeting from -- of people from the Dukagjini Zone but not of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Exactly. Can I take it you've never seen the minutes to that meeting then or studied them yourself?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Very well. The minutes record -- or at least one version of the minutes records that Rexhep Selimi, who was I think at that point a member of the General Staff, was present at that meeting. Is that something that you are aware of or not, that there was one member of the General Staff present at that meeting? If you can't remember, please say so.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about this later from Rexhep Selimi himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, you also mentioned a meeting of the General Staff at which a decision was taken concerning the appointment of the commander of the Dukagjini region and I think you mentioned two locations for it according to my notes. You had mentioned Klecka and also Divjake, D-i-v-j-a-k-e, just a few moments ago in answer to Judge Hoepfel. Wherever the meeting of the General Staff took place, can we assume or can we infer from your evidence, that that was a meeting that took place after the election of Ramush Haradinaj on the 23rd of June?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. We took into account the decision of the zone because the zone brought the proposal and we decided on the proposals that the zone sent us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. And just for the sake of the record, what -- can you now remember was it at Divjake or Klecka that that meeting took place? Can you remember at which of the two it was? Again, if you can't remember, please say so.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Klecka and Divjake are very close to each other, but as far as I remember it was in Divjake.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Very well. And finally this: You've called it an appointment rather than an election in answer to Judge Hoepfel's question. Does it really come to this that you were presented with the results of an election and you endorsed those results, you, the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was a decision that was made in the Dukagjini Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes. And do you know roughly how long after the election your meeting took place in Klecka?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly, but I could venture a week or ten days after that meeting. Could have been more or less than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there are no further questions triggered by the questions of the Bench, do we need - and I am addressing the parties - do we need the presence of the witness to deal with the books? Perhaps we should ask the witness. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are three books on my table which were provided by Mr. Kearney. One bears a title in English which is: "Kosova in a historical context." And if the parties would not object, I would read that the title in original would be: Kosova [Interpretation] "In a historical context." [In English] Is that the original in your language? Is that the book you wrote?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have another book, which I can't give you the title of, but it seems that it is, at least, the cover is in off-white and something between red and pink with a picture of a statue. Is that a book that you wrote?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there is a third book which is with a green cover and I would say a picture of what we know as P Exhibit 9, that is, a UCK emblem on it. Is that a book you wrote?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not my book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So therefore, that is an -- is that a book published by a person by the name of Gafur Elshani?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is it a collection of documents and articles?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have identified the three books that were provided by the Office of the Prosecution. The books you wrote, when you wrote them, did you intend to give a -- on the assumption that you wrote about the events in the late 1990s in Kosovo, was it your intention to write historical documents which would reflect your view on what happened at the time?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave information about the events that happened from 1990 to 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And in your recollection, did you try to do your best to reflect facts as good as you could in accordance with the facts that took place at the time?

utterances.speaker: JAKUP KRASNIQI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was my aim, so that the readers in Kosova could get to know about a very difficult period in their history.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. I don't want to take this any further, just to see whether Mr. Krasniqi wanted to write a novel -- well, with -- where he felt totally free to mix up history and other things. This is not just for the information of the parties. A question -- at least the answer to the question does not mean that everything Mr. Krasniqi wrote in the book is the ultimate statement of the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wasn't going to raise the issue at this stage because I think it's apparent as it possibly could be from the cross-examination of this witness that a mixture of statements where the sources on examination prove not to be as reliable as the statements might appear has been characteristic of his writings in certain cases, not least because he was engaged in the promulgation of propaganda. And so before anything in the books became material on which the Tribunal would want to proceed, it would presumably be necessary to have Mr. Krasniqi recalled to examine --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- of course I just wanted to know whether he intended to write fiction or whether he intended to at least deal with history, even if that would leave quite some room for interpreting history. Then I'd like to give the three books back to the Prosecution, and the Chamber at this moment will not further deal with the books unless the parties would refer to it. Then, Mr. Krasniqi, this then concludes your evidence. You may have understood that since the parties had not yet read the three books, that they might apply at any later stage that you would further testify about what they find in the books. The Chamber doesn't know whether this will happen or not, but this is just to inform you that I could not exclude for that possibility. I'd like to thank you for having come to The Hague and to have answered questions of the parties and the Bench and I wish you a safe trip home again. I'm just consulting the parties. I think under the present circumstances an instruction not to say a word about his testimony would not be appropriate. I see that the parties agree with me, so I'll not give such an instruction at this moment. Then one final matter. Is there any objection against P329, that is, the map tendered by Mr. Kearney. No objection. Then P329 is admitted into evidence. Since protective measures have to be prepared for the next witness, we will -- Madam Registrar, do we need then a full half-hour to prepare for -- especially for voice distortion? Yes. Then we'll resume -- Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Mr. Di Fazio will be taking the next witness assisted by Ms. Schweiger. I just wish to -- I note the Trial Chamber's decision in relation to provision of cross-examination material. I just wish to draw the Defence counsel, if they haven't received it, their attention to the disposition on the final page and having to provide material when the witness takes an oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That will take another half-hour, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm standing here. I hadn't even realised that the Trial Chamber had issued that decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It had been signed at 3.00 today; it has been filed a half an hour ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's clearly not something we can implement for the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not blamed for -- to the extent possible because that's -- the decision, as a matter of fact, follows the Milutinovic decision in this respect. That means that exhibits to be used in cross-examination should be announced at the beginning of the testimony of the witness in chief, that is, when he takes the oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So on from the moment where there's no further free communication between the Prosecution and the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To the extent possible, of course, you're invited to -- to meet with the new decision -- but there's full understanding that preparation within one hour, within half an hour, risks shortcomings which are understandable.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, I am looking at you, you would certainly understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We certainly do but would there anything to prevent the Defence from complying with the spirit of it by providing the material by tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although -- yes. That --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'd like to study the decision before I respond to any of it and see the terms in which it's been put. Whilst --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Literally the same as Milutinovic. If we need the witness for what you would like to raise, then we'll ask him to stay; but otherwise, I would rather -- it's a quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I can deal with it in one sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Re and I have spoken about the issue of timetable for the Defence objections in respect of the subpoena for Witness 730.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no objection to the Defence filing that which it wishes to file on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and Mr. Re, there would be no problem since, I'm talking off the top of my head, that on the 18th of June that witness is supposed to testify. That would not cause you any problems in view of the time it usually takes to -- first of all, for the Chamber to decide, then to have it translated, have it given --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's no difficulty, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No difficulty. Then we'll have a break and we'll resume at quarter past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, you are on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I am. I'm sorry to be but I am. I just wanted to bring one thing to the Trial Chamber's attention. The 92 ter summaries have not been read in yet for the last witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'm happy to do it at another time, I'm happy to do it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd rather do it at a moment when there's no witness waiting. It's to inform the public but not necessarily to be done immediately on the spot. Mr. Di Fazio, is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness? MR. DI FAZIO: It is ready, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that would be Witness 6? Protective measures, face distortion, voice distortion, and pseudonym. Is that -- MR. DI FAZIO: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Usher, could you take the necessary measures to get the witness into the courtroom. I take it that it goes without saying that the cameras will also respect the face distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Will your -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I apologise for interrupting. I didn't realise the Trial Chamber was conferring. Will Your Honours explain the measures that apply in respect of protection of this witness to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I usually say something about it especially when I address him as Witness 6. MR. DI FAZIO: I would be grateful if you could. I haven't had a chance to speak to this man, and so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- he'll probably be reassured to know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I will pay attention to it. MR. DI FAZIO: And just before that last statement leads me into any error, let me say this: I tried to speak to this man moments ago without the assistance of an interpreter and I think that I probably ended up causing more bewilderment than anything else and I wanted to explain the court system and therefore I want that set clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness 6. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, only in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness 6, I call you Witness 6 because the Chamber has decided that protective measures were justified in respect of you. That means that we'll not use your own name, we'll call you Witness 6; no one outside this courtroom would see your face, even those who are on the public gallery will not see your face because they're -- it's shielded, as you can see; furthermore, your voice is distorted, that means when your testimony is broadcasted that no one will see your face but also no one will be able to recognise your voice. Do you understand that? Yes. Then before you give evidence the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher and I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will first be examined by Mr. Di Fazio, who's counsel for the Prosecution. Don't be worried, the curtains will be up but the screen is still there, so that no one sees your face. Mr. Di Fazio, once the curtains have stopped making noise, you may proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Examination by Mr. Di Fazio:

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness 6, I'm going to show you something on the screen that appears in front of you. MR. DI FAZIO: I'd like the witness to be shown 65 ter 1347, which I believe is his pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness, feel free to lean forward and have a look, and I'd like you to look at the details that are contained on that document. And without mentioning them out loud, can you tell us if the last -- if that is your last name; if that is your first name; your father's name; your date of birth; and your place of birth. Are those details correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: I'd just like to get some more personal details from this witness, and if Your Honours please we'll have to go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session. Witness 6, that means even what you say could not be heard by anyone outside this courtroom. May I invite you to come a bit closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Madam Registrar, could I assume that 65 ter number 1347 would be P330?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And since I expect no objections, it's admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: And under seal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Under seal, yes, of course. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for reminding me. MR. DI FAZIO: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Witness, I want you to turn your mind to events in June of 1998. Now, in that month did you visit any relatives or attempt to visit any relatives?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, again it's important that you don't mention names so that you're not identified. Where were these relatives living at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6
utterances.text: In Nepole village, Peje municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And were these relatives, in fact, of your wife?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6
utterances.text: Family, my wife's family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Did you attempt -- did you, in fact, start out on a journey to visit these people?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, every question so far has been leading and I have not objected, but from here on in I would ask that Mr. Di Fazio exercise extreme caution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, you're put at notice. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, my question was: Did you visit these people? I'm asking you about the month of June 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the question was: Did you start out on a visit to these people?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Unless there's any specific reason whether starting out here would not have resulted in visiting, I think we could have done without the objection, but if there's any good reason for that I do not know, but Mr. Di Fazio certainly will know. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: In June 1998 did you visit any relatives?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6
utterances.text: No. We set out to visit them but we were stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Who did you set out to visit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6
utterances.text: I set out with my wife and my five children and we were going to visit my wife's family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. How did you set out? How were you travelling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6
utterances.text: We set out by car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Whose car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6
utterances.text: My car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6
utterances.text: A Mercedes Benz.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was in the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6
utterances.text: I was with my wife and my five children. My wife was pregnant at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, cast your mind back and tell us, if you can, if you can, the date upon which you set out on this trip.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6
utterances.text: It was the 13th. It was a Friday in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And just again, in case it's not absolutely clear, what month was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6
utterances.text: The sixth month.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you arrive at your destination?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Without mentioning the name of your home village, tell us the route upon which you set out on this trip.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6
utterances.text: It was about 11.30 a.m. when we set out from my village towards the village of my wife's family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What road did you take in order to get to the village of your wife's family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6
utterances.text: The Gjakove-Kline road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: What sort of road is that? Is that a secondary road, a principal road? Can you inform the Trial Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6
utterances.text: It is a main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: How far did you get along that road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6
utterances.text: Up to a place called Grabanice. The Serbian military stopped us there. We returned and took the direction towards my house. It was about 1.00 when they kidnapped me on the Gjakove-Kline main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I'm going to get to that issue of what you say is your kidnapping in a moment, but firstly I want to be clear about the route that you took. When you left your home village, did you get on to the main Djakovica-Klina road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: And did you travel northwards along that road in the direction of your wife's family's village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct because my village is at the exit from Gjakove. It's from there that I took the direction towards my wife's family village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Now, I want to be absolutely sure. On what road was this Serb location where the military -- Serbian military stopped you? It's the road that I'm interested. Where was this -- where was the Serb military that you have mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. MR. DI FAZIO: Your Honours, I was wondering if the Defence have no objection, would they mind the witness being given a map for him to look at overnight. He may be, by given time for him to look at it, be able to mark his itinerary on such a map and it may be that this will resolve the matter. And I'm sure that all the parties are interested in knowing exactly where he was stopped and how. So that's a suggestion I make, it's made in the spirit of trying to clarify what I think is a noncontentious area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And would then the map do, the map that we have in front of us with the red circles on it. Witness 6 -- yes, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I ask that the witness remove his headphones for just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you take off your headphones for just a second. Yes, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no means of knowing the answer to this question but I thought I should at least raise it. The witness has for the first time in a -- and he's made something like eight statements to my knowledge. He has for the first time today mentioned this business about having been stopped by a Serb roadblock. It is in the statement of his wife, and so obviously I'm not taken by surprise by it. I have no means of knowing whether his wife is here with him in The Hague. If she were, then of course it would be fatuous to suggest that he wouldn't speak to her overnight, and if he's going to take a map home with him --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, not to -- I wouldn't instruct the witness not to speak to his wife until tomorrow but certainly give an additional --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I just thought I should ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Di Fazio, do you know whether the witness is accompanied by his -- MR. DI FAZIO: I don't know. I don't know that detail. I wish I could answer you now I just don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I rather doubt it but I can't say one way or the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll ask the witness in such a way that -- Witness 6, could you please put your earphones on again. Witness 6, did you come to The Hague with any members of your family or did you come alone? If you came with members of your family, don't tell me who it is, but did you come alone or are family members accompanying you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am alone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That -- then, Witness 6, the map you see on your screen at this moment --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I think I see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we are going to do is the following. We are going to provide you with a similar map on paper. If you would please, before you return in this courtroom tomorrow, carefully look at that map on paper and try for yourself to find out what roads you exactly took on the day you have been asked questions about so that tomorrow we might more easily find our way on this map. So you'll be provided with a paper copy of the map. You should not consult other people about it, but just for yourself to look at it to see whether you can find the villages, the roads where you went so that tomorrow you're prepared to answer further questions on this subject. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to say something, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you would like to say something. Please tell me and tell the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to speak about my kidnapping from Guri i Zi, that place, everything is in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will continue tomorrow putting further questions to you. We usually stop at 7.00 at night. And since you have, from what I understand, given several statements, it might be that the Chamber would like to hear from you and not just read what you earlier gave as a statement.
